requirements.moduleTitle: Foundational FSVP Framework, Statutory Authority & Scope

statutoryRules.rule: U.S. Importer must be determined according to 21 CFR 1.500 (U.S. owner or consignee with financial interest at entry).
A written hazard analysis must be conducted or evaluated for each food imported (21 CFR 1.504).
Appropriate verification activities must be established and conducted for each foreign supplier (21 CFR 1.506).
When a food has a hazard with SAHC potential, an annual onsite audit of the foreign supplier is mandatory unless an alternative is scientifically justified (21 CFR 1.506(d)(1)).

messages.text: Please answer my earlier unanswered consultant question above. Do not attach any documents.

My apologies for the earlier confusion, Husni. To answer your question, we currently have two primary counterparties involved in this supply chain: Amman Food Packers and Beirut Freight Forwarder. We are certain that these two entities are our partners. Based on our general operations, Amman Food Packers is responsible for supplying and packing the Mediterranean specialty foods we import, while Beirut Freight Forwarder handles the logistics and shipping of these goods to the U.S.

As for what we may need to verify internally: while we know Amman Food Packers supplies our goods, we will need to confirm whether they actually manufacture all of the products—such as the olive oil, halva, za'atar, and tahini—or if they simply consolidate and pack items from other local farms and facilities. We are also uncertain how the FDA specifically classifies these entities under the FSVP rules, such as which one is technically considered our 'foreign supplier' for compliance purposes.

messages.text: For the two counterparties you identified earlier, please clarify the specific business role each one plays in relation to Levant. Also distinguish what you know as an established business fact from anything you are only assuming or still need to verify. Do not attach any documents.

Husni, to clarify and formalize the specific business roles based on our established business facts: It is a confirmed fact that Amman Food Packers acts as our direct supplier. Their established role is to supply and pack the Mediterranean specialty foods, including the olive oil, halva, za'atar, and tahini that we import. It is also an established fact that Beirut Freight Forwarder acts as our consolidator and logistics provider; their role is strictly to handle the freight forwarding and shipping of these goods to the United States.

In terms of what we are assuming or still need to verify: While it is a fact that Amman Food Packers supplies and packs the goods for us, we are currently only assuming that they manufacture all of these items themselves. We still need to verify internally whether they actually produce the foods at their own facility, or if they are simply consolidating and packing products manufactured by other local farms or facilities. We also need your guidance to determine how these roles translate to FDA definitions, specifically which entity is technically considered the 'foreign supplier' for our FSVP compliance.
